closest_prior_work.citation: Padmanabhan, D. & Natarajan, K. (2021). Tree Bounds for Sums of Bernoulli Random Variables: A Linear Optimization Approach. INFORMS Journal on Optimization 3(1), 23-45.
closest_prior_work.difference: Already studies tightest bounds on P(sum of dependent Bernoullis exceeds k) from univariate/bivariate information; this paper applies the complete-pair LP empirically to ECMWF temperature portfolios rather than developing tractable/tree methods.

closest_prior_work.citation: Boros, E. & Prekopa, A. (1989). Closed Form Two-Sided Bounds for Probabilities that At Least r and Exactly r Out of n Events Occur. Mathematics of Operations Research 14(2), 317-342.
closest_prior_work.difference: Provides classical tight bounds for at-least-r events from aggregated/binomial moments; this paper differs by also retaining all individual margins and measuring widths on operational forecasts.

closest_prior_work.citation: Ramachandra, A.K. & Natarajan, K. (2023). Tight Probability Bounds with Pairwise Independence. SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics 37(2), 516-555.
closest_prior_work.difference: Reviews the general bivariate-information LP and aggregated-moment bounds; its pairwise-independence specialization does not apply here, and this paper adds an empirical weather audit.

closest_prior_work.citation: Giglio, S. (2016). Credit Default Swap Spreads and Systemic Financial Risk. ESRB Working Paper No. 15.
closest_prior_work.difference: Empirically derives tightest bounds on many simultaneous defaults because individual and pairwise probabilities do not characterize multiple-default risk; this paper is the analogous count-tail LP exercise for ensemble temperature exceedances, with fully observed ensemble pairs.

closest_prior_work.citation: Schefzik, R., Thorarinsdottir, T.L. & Gneiting, T. (2013). Uncertainty Quantification in Complex Simulation Models Using Ensemble Copula Coupling. Statistical Science 28, 616-640.
closest_prior_work.difference: ECC restores dependence by reordering calibrated margins using a raw-ensemble rank template; this paper instead quantifies worst-case partial identification and only uses a historical-rank template as one point-reconstruction control.

main_issues.issue: Headline pair near-identification (width 0.0547, 1,068/2,871 identified) is conditional on exact moments of a finite 50-member empirical law with exact zero pair cells and few surviving patterns; a 0.005 arbitrary-weight allowance raises width to 0.1858 and larger/smoother ensembles are untested, so it does not establish identification for an underlying forecast distribution.

No real constrained delivery product, user, observation verification, or health/economic outcome is shown: ECMWF members are available at source, thresholds and capacities are stylized, and certification is only self-consistency with the same ensemble law.

Methodological novelty is minimal: the atom LP, nested tightening, aggregate binomial-moment bounds and insufficiency of pairs for higher-order events are classical and acknowledged, leaving only an empirical application.

Generality is narrow: 28 matched dates in one 2026 season, convenience centres, two spacings, 12 sites, two products/leads and fixed absolute thresholds; informative pair widths already vary 0.0187-0.1084 across geometry-by-lead cells.

The primary arbitrary-weight LP does not match the known 50 equal-weight ensemble it summarises; the integer check covers only 120 selected queries (11/120 aggregate endpoints unresolved, and 26 unresolved at radius 0.02), so the operationally relevant feasible class is only partially characterised.

Headline rates are composition-sensitive: 3,941 tails are 0 and 3,469 are 1 and 5,064 queries have at most two uncertain sites; the informative and near-threshold strata condition on the target q, and at cost ratio 0.1 the informative filter itself determines the weakly optimal action.

Reproduction from the paper alone is incomplete: exact centres, thresholds, capacity fractions and seeds are deferred to bundled protocol/VERIFY/claims files not inspectable in the manuscript, and several appendix tables have overlapping/garbled numbers in the PDF.
The abstract and manuscript are overloaded with exploratory appendices and caveats, burying the primary estimand and making the usable takeaway hard to extract.

research_question.predictable_reason: Nested releases must weakly narrow by construction, and finite-support zero cells make strong pair identification plausible, but the empirical magnitudes (0.51/0.31/0.055) and 43.4% aggregate share were not predetermined.
research_question.question: For fixed 12-site portfolios in operational ECMWF forecasts, how tightly do marginal, marginal-plus-aggregate-second-moment, and marginal-plus-all-pairwise summaries bound P(at least k sites exceed a temperature threshold), and how often do they certify an illustrative cost-loss action?

score_reasons.clarity: Glossary and explicit denominators help, but the abstract, 20 pages and appendices A-M overload the primary result with exploratory diagnostics and some appendix tables render garbled.
score_reasons.correctness: LP bounds are sharp by construction, solver residuals and structural sensitivities are checked, and claims are carefully limited to the empirical ensemble law; remaining concerns are interpretation, not evident arithmetic errors.
score_reasons.generality: One season, 28 matched dates, 12 sites, two spacings/products/leads and 50 members, with pair performance driven by finite support, do not support transfer to larger ensembles, other spacings, hazards or smoothed laws.
score_reasons.novelty: The count-tail LP and moment bounds are classical, e.g. tight Bernoulli-sum bounds from marginal/bivariate information and Boros-Prekopa aggregate bounds; novelty is only the specific empirical comparison, not found within the range searched.
score_reasons.usefulness: Usefully warns product designers that margins under-determine joint counts and that count distributions/binary masks are cheap exact alternatives, but no real user constraint, calibrated event or observed outcome is evaluated.
score_reasons.verifiability: Detailed provenance, hashes, solver checks, VERIFY.md and claims mapping are described, but exact design values and artifacts are outside the paper text, so results cannot be fully audited from the manuscript alone.

strengths: Sharp, well-specified partial-identification LP with primal/dual residual checks and explicit separation of arbitrary-weight versus known-50-equal-weight feasible classes.
Prespecified informative stratum and full denominators expose floor/ceiling and few-uncertain-site cases that make all-query averages look artificially good.
Strong sensitivity suite: integer lattice equivalence, moment perturbation, controlled exact-margin comparisons, common-query member-size checks and repeated member draws.
Intellectually honest scoping: distinguishes compatibility width from midpoint point error, identification from forecast skill, and makes no health, economic or network-saving claim.
review.summary: A careful empirical partial-identification audit: on 12,096 12-site ECMWF queries, marginal/aggregate/pair releases give mean compatible widths 0.141/0.089/0.014 overall and 0.514/0.315/0.055 in 2,871 informative queries, with pairs certifying most illustrative actions only under exact finite-ensemble moments. The execution and caveating are unusually thorough, but the LP is classical, the practical delivery constraint is hypothetical, pair near-identification is largely a finite-support/exact-moment artefact, and generalisation beyond the sampled 50-member, one-season, stylised portfolios is weak.
